judge_context: Must update the existing proof summary (ps_001) for q_001 in place — there must be exactly one proof_summary for q_001 afterward, never a duplicate (ps_002) for the same question
Should keep the conclusion coherent with the existing evidence (probable tier unless the underlying evidence basis actually changed)

A refinement presented in the reply MUST be the persisted one. Observed 2026-08-21: the reply narrated a reviewed and refined summary while ps_001.narrative_markdown was left byte-identical, only the metadata fields changing. The deliverable is the persisted entry; prose that exists only in chat is not a refinement, and claiming one that was not written is a Correctness failure, not a presentation nit. Finding nothing worth changing in the narrative is a fine outcome — say that instead.

Score `Tree encoding` NULL (N/A) on this test. The concluded parentage is ALREADY encoded in the scenario's pre-state — `mid-research-flynn`'s tree carries R1 (ParentChild I2 to I1) with three source-refs, and I1's Birth fact F1 is already `primary: true` — so this run has nothing to mark and makes no tree call. Do NOT score 3: that credits the skill for the fixture's own pre-state. Do NOT score 1 or 2: there is no found-but-lost failure to catch when the conclusion is already on the tree. Observed on constant behaviour across six runs, this cell read 3, 2, 1, 1, 3, 3 and twice cost the test its pass. THIS IS A PER-TEST INSTRUCTION AND DOES NOT GENERALIZE FROM THE `no-new-proof-expected` TAG: an updated `probable` conclusion whose concluded value is NOT already on the tree must still reach it, which is exactly what the rubric's `no-new-proof-expected` paragraph protects.
